narrations.en: Step 16 (Final Step): The visual proof is complete! Starting from the starting condition of applying a linear transformation that changes a11, the x component of the 1-column basis vector e1(1,0) of the matrix, to the unit square area of the coordinate plane, which was the starting condition, instead of inserting countless points inside the area one by one, the horizontal reference arrow e1=(1,0) and the vertical reference arrow e2=(0,1) go through the base arrow auxiliary line that tracks which coordinates the two basis vectors move to, and then the matrix components. It was clearly confirmed that, depending on the value of a11, the x-component of the first-column basis vector e1(1,0), a geometric transformation law is established that creates horizontal stretching and y-axis symmetrical reflection (a11<0), which extends or reduces the geometric area in the horizontal (x-axis) direction of the unit square grid while fixing the vertical axis. The key point to remember here is that if you try to solve a linear transformation problem only by substituting complex simultaneous equations, it is easy to get lost! Always observe first as a geometric basis shift that (1,0) moves to the first column and (0,1) moves to the second column. Finally, ask a deeper question. If the two column vectors of the matrix lie on a straight line and the parallelogram is distorted into flat line segments (determinant a11a22 - a12a21 = 0), why can't there be an inverse transformation (inverse matrix)?
